sources.entry: RAG Learning Academy by Taka Goto - A multi-agent Claude Code learning environment for mastering Retrieval-Augmented Generation, with 20 specialist agents, 22 slash commands, and a 9-module hands-on curriculum that runs zero-config inside Claude Code. Quality is evident — 616 tests, CI, and weekly/monthly content-freshness automation that opens issues for stale material.

summary.one_liner: A Claude Code-based interactive learning environment with 20 specialist agents, 22 slash commands, and a 9-module hands-on curriculum for learning Retrieval-Augmented Generation.
summary.what_it_does: Turns Claude Code into a RAG tutor: you run /start to be assessed into a track (Beginner, Intermediate, or Advanced) and then work through lessons covering document processing, chunking, embeddings, vector databases (Chroma, Pinecone, pgvector), retrieval strategies (dense, sparse, hybrid, reranking, MMR), prompt engineering and grounding, evaluation (RAGAS and retrieval/generation metrics), and advanced and production patterns. Each concept is paired with an exercise and evaluation criteria. The repo includes slash commands for quizzes, building components, evaluating pipelines, debugging failures, comparing approaches, and tracking progress through milestones and proficiency levels. A `make dashboard` command generates an HTML progress page. The default stack is local and needs no API keys: Claude Code as the LLM, all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings, ChromaDB, LangChain, and RAGAS. The README also describes content-freshness checks that flag outdated material through hooks and CI.
use_cases: learn retrieval-augmented generation step by step
build a first RAG pipeline over my own documents
compare chunking, embedding, and retrieval approaches
evaluate RAG quality with RAGAS-style metrics
prepare a RAG system for production deployment
guided RAG study plan inside Claude Code
how_to_run: git clone <repository URL> (the README leaves the URL blank)
notable: Multi-agent design: 20 agents across director, domain lead, and specialist tiers, invoked on request rather than auto-routed
Each lesson is tagged core or optional, with a core path of about 8.5 hours to a working, evaluated RAG system
Content freshness automation: frontmatter review cycles, session hook warnings, monthly CI issue tracking, and an optional local routine that opens PRs
Zero-config start: no API keys or pip install needed up front; dependencies are installed when a lesson needs them
Test suite of 700+ structural and content tests run through make ci
caveats: Full curriculum takes about 31 hours; the core path is about 8.5 hours
Running Ollama locally needs 8-16GB RAM for LLMs, and the README warns heavy apps may need closing
The freshness routine's launchd install is macOS-only, and the local routine depends on a maintainer's Claude Code subscription
The README clone command has no URL filled in
